message: In the concealed under-deck support frame (C2), Structural Dynamics Lead, the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) mounting and access has risk of changing the deck view or fouling the moving mass. To check it I used layout reasoning (the concealed mounting cross-section (E7)) building on the side-view mode-shape layout (the side-view mode-shape layout (E3)). I found two 200 kilogram masses fit between fixed girders below the soffit with 30 millimetre clearance for 8.2 millimetre stroke from the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6), with no fixings through the wearing surface, according to Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures (HIVOSS), 2008. I propose bolted cross-frames with lockable hatches accessed from below and soffit-matched finish. My position: not ready because connection loads need team review. In the deck-view preservation detail, Vibration Control Specialist, the parapet voids and deck surface have risk of visual intrusion from fixings or covers. To check it I used visibility review (the concealed mounting cross-section (E7)) and the optimal TMD sizing (the optimal TMD sizing (E4)). I found zero change above deck level with all hardware below soffit at 1.86 Hertz tuning, according to HIVOSS, 2008. I propose no deck penetration and concealed cable routing below. My position: not ready because finishes need agreement.
